transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-16
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortega (Redwood CSM), Daniel Brooks (Atlas CTO), Maya Singh (Atlas ML), Liam O'Connor (Atlas Infra), Sofia Ramos (Atlas Security)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Showed how to pivot from a failing request to traces, identify root cause (quantization mismatch + tokenization edge-case), and export request logs for offline analysis. Discussed retention, SSO/KMS requirements, and next steps for a short pilot.

Topics: console tracing UI, error analysis flow, request logs export, debug traces, trace sampling, retention & compliance, dedicated vs hosted routing, benchmark plan

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, with Priya on the demo side. How's everyone doin?
[00:08] Daniel: Good, thanks. Excited to see the tracing stuff — we've had some opaque failures in staging.
[00:13] Priya: Great, we'll jump into the Console tracing area — show error analysis and request logs. I'll share my screen.
[00:20] Maya: quick note — we mostly run GPT-style open models but are evaluating quantized Llama variants. Performance is huge for us.
[00:28] Priya: got it, that matters for how KV cache and quantization interact.
[00:35] [screen share starts] Priya: ok at the top left is the Tracing tab, you can filter by model, route, and time range. We'll load a failing request example.
[00:48] Priya: there's a trace timeline, each span shows token-generation latency, model variant, and any fallback events. Notice this one — you can see a spike at token 87.
[01:05] Liam: is that tokenization or model compute?
[01:08] Priya: at first glance it looks like compute — but if you click the span you get metadata: request_id, trace_id, model_variant, quantization profile, hardware type (A100-v4), and a short stack: 'decode->kv_lookup->generate'.
[01:28] Priya: sometimes the product name shows incorrectly in transcripts; the Console is the right place.
[01:33] Daniel: heh, yep. How accurate is the trace timing? We need sub-20ms token timing for p99 analysis.
[01:40] Priya: timings are captured at the runtime level — we show per-span ms and p50/p95/p99 histograms. For p99 we're within the instrumentation accuracy — we also show host-level metrics to correlate GPU queueing.
[01:53] [02:00] Priya: right now I'm toggling error analysis — it groups similar failing traces by signature. You can see 'decode-error: token-split' and a separate group for 'oom-fallback'.
[02:15] Maya: that token-split signature — is that from tokenizer mismatch between model and our client?
[02:19] Priya: often yes. We attach inputs and pretokenized lengths to the trace so you can compare client-side tokenization. In this example the client sent a stray zero-width space, so token-boundary changed mid-sequence.
[02:35] Daniel: ok that explains weird hallucinations we've seen.
[02:40] Priya: from the error group you can 'drill into sample traces' and then open the full request log. The Request Logs panel stores the full request/response payloads (subject to redaction policy) and you can export a csv or ndjson.
[02:55] Liam: what's retention? We can't keep PII longer than 90 days.
[02:59] Priya: retention is configurable per-account tier: Hosted default is 30 days, Dedicated can be 90/365 or customer-managed in Private with your KMS. We also support field-level redaction and custom retention windows — Priya: I'll drop the doc link later.
[03:15] Sofia: about KMS — can we use our HSM and do envelope encryption?
[03:19] Priya: yes, for Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS/HSM, and Dedicated has KMS integrations for enterprise. I'll flag the security deck for Alex to share.
[03:30] [03:35] Alex: quick pause — a lot of folks ask about sampling. We can collect all traces for a route or do adaptive sampling (higher for errors). That keeps costs reasonable.
[03:47] Priya: demo continuing — here's request id 9f4a... you can see timeline, logs, model events, kernel switching note (we fell back to a quantized kernel for memory).
[04:00] Maya: when it falls back to quantized kernel, do we see quality regressions?
[04:05] Priya: we surface a quality score delta computed from your eval set if attached — in this session we had a small BLEU-ish delta for the failing group. Also Optimize recommendations will flag when quantization causes high regression for a prompt set.
[04:23] [04:30] Priya: I'm now showing the 'Compare traces' feature — you can align two traces side-by-side and diff token outputs. Useful for A/B between hq and quantized model.
[04:42] Liam: that would help triage before we flip production.
[04:46] Priya: exactly. Next, Request Logs export — you can apply filters (route, status, response time, error signature) and export an ndjson. There's a pre-built query for 'p99 latency > 1s' which we use to investigate tail latency.
[05:02] Daniel: good. For auditing, we need immutable export and a signed hash.
[05:08] Priya: Dedicated and Private support retention snapshots and signed export bundles for compliance. We'll send the export spec.
[05:16] [05:30] Priya: now a quick live debug — running a synthetic request that previously failed. We'll attach CPU/GPU metrics and host logs.
[05:42] [06:00] Priya: you can see host GPU utilization spiked, and the trace shows a kernel compile happening earlier which increased latencies. That was the root cause here — cold kernel compile + burst in concurrent requests.
[06:18] Maya: could autoscaling have prevented that?
[06:22] Priya: yes, Dedicated autoscaling and primed kernels help. For hosted we do warm-pool priming heuristics but a large, sudden spike can expose compile times. We recommend canary deploys and pre-warming for major model flips.
[06:37] [07:00] Alex: quick commercial note — for predictable throughput and avoiding warm compiles, teams often move to Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[07:08] Daniel: price delta? We'll need the spreadsheet.
[07:11] Alex: will send.
[07:15] [07:30] Priya: jumping back — here's an example of a trace linked to a user-facing error. The console shows 'user-visible error: truncated-output' and the request log shows the client closed the stream early.
[07:45] Daniel: sometimes we get truncated outputs but client says connection ok. Is there a way to link network layer events?
[07:52] Priya: yes we ingest network events when the client uses our SDKs or if you forward proxy logs. That linkage is visible in the trace timeline.
[08:03] [08:30] Priya: another useful tool is 'Alerts from traces' — you can create metric alerts based on trace signatures (e.g., token-split rate > 0.5%).
[08:43] Liam: can those trigger webhooks into PagerDuty?
[08:46] Priya: yes, we have webhooks, Slack, PagerDuty integrations.
[08:53] [09:00] Maya: on the technical side, do traces include KV cache hit/miss counts?
[09:04] Priya: yes, we surface KV cache stats per request and aggregate across routes. You'll see hit ratio and average lookup latency.
[09:14] [09:30] Priya: ok I'm going to show how to annotate traces and open a bug right from the console — you can attach trace id, sample logs, and assign to an owner.
[09:45] [10:00] Daniel: that integrates with our JIRA?
[10:03] Priya: we have webhook-based ticket creation; setting up takes a few mins.
[10:10] [10:30] Sam: quick commercial Q — in a POC would we hand over dedicated keys?
[10:35] Alex: for POCs we usually offer a short Dedicated eval or Hosted with a restricted retention and RBAC. For Private you can bring your own keys.
[10:47] [11:00] Priya: jumping to request-logs debugging — here's an ndjson export with redaction applied, you can run local tooling.
[11:10] Maya: are attachments preserved (like images passed to multimodal models)?
[11:15] Priya: we store references and content based on your retention and privacy settings; for Private you control storage. For Hosted we recommend offloading large blobs to customer S3 via signed URLs.
[11:28] [12:00] Priya: small transcription note — Console sometimes displays model name 'RW-infer' in short, that's an internal alias in some logs.
[12:10] Daniel: fine as long as mapping exists.
[12:15] [12:30] Priya: switching to Error Analysis panel — you can create a dataset from failing traces to run evals. We'll show how Optimize ties in to recommend quant profiles or batching settings.
[12:42] Maya: can Optimize recommend token batch sizes per-route? We have mixed short and long sequences.
[12:47] Priya: yes, Optimize analyzes sequence length distribution and suggests batching configs, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles per workload.
[12:58] [13:30] Priya: now a short deep dive — let's look at a trace where the model switched kernels mid-request due to memory. You can see the kernel note and fallback event.
[13:47] Maya: does that switching cause context corruption?
[13:50] Priya: rare, but possible with early kernels — runtime does KV reconciliation to prevent corruption, and we flag suspected token shifts.
[14:02] [14:30] Priya: discussing traces for multi-tenant vs single-tenant: we tag traces by customer account and route and you can scoping to team-level with RBAC.
[14:45] Sofia: needed — we require SSO + SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC.
[14:50] Alex: we support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC lets you limit access to traces by role. We'll share the security checklist.
[15:05] [15:30] Priya: showing the Audit Logs view — every trace access and export is logged, with who accessed which trace and when. That satisfies SOC2 audit trails.
[15:45] Daniel: nice.
[15:50] [16:00] Priya: ok returning to request logs — you can search by request_id, user_id, trace_id, or custom tags. We auto-inject trace_id into SDK logs.
[16:15] Maya: we use a custom user id header; can that be indexed?
[16:19] Priya: yes, custom headers can be promoted to indexed fields in Request Logs for faster querying.
[16:30] [17:00] Priya: quick demo of live tail — you can tail requests in real-time and apply filters. Useful during deploy windows.
[17:12] Liam: does tailing add overhead to latency?
[17:15] Priya: no, tailing reads from the event stream; overhead is minimal, but collecting full payloads can increase storage.
[17:24] [18:00] Alex: commercial again — if you want, we can provision a dedicated dev cluster for your team to run realistic load tests.
[18:10] Daniel: yes that'd help.
[18:14] [18:30] Priya: showing sample trace annotation and how to open a support ticket from inside. We also have SDKs that can attach local debug logs to a trace id.
[18:42] Maya: great, that would let us correlate client-side logs with server traces.
[18:47] [19:00] Priya: now quick Q&A — Daniel: are there limits on request-log export size?
[19:07] Priya: exports are chunked; large exports are staged to a customer S3 export location or a signed bundle.
[19:15] Sofia: regulatory question: can we limit export to EU-region storage only?
[19:21] Priya: yes, region controls are available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted region options depend on cloud region selection.
[19:33] [20:00] Daniel: for the benchmark we plan — what's recommended load pattern?
[20:07] Priya: run a 48h mixed-load with your short/long sequence mix, sample traces for p99 tail latency and error signatures; record concurrent users and peak qps. We'll analyze and provide a report.
[20:25] [21:00] Maya: do you need us to wrap requests with trace headers?
[21:05] Priya: use our SDK which auto-injects trace headers, or add X-Trace-Id header manually.
[21:12] [22:00] Alex: ok wrapping up, quick recap.
[22:06] Alex: action items: send pricing, share recording and docs, Atlas to run benchmark and share traces, security checklist followup.
[22:15] Daniel: good. Couple final Qs — what about model rollback policies in Console?
[22:22] Priya: we support rollouts with canary, A/B, auto-fallback to previous model if errors exceed thresholds; rollouts are visible in Console with trace-linked comparisons.
[22:36] Liam: do rollbacks keep in-flight requests consistent?
[22:40] Priya: yes, we route new requests based on config; in-flight are allowed to finish.
[22:47] [23:00] Sam: I'll log a follow-up for procurement once Atlas wants Dedicated pricing.
[23:06] Alex: perfect.
[23:10] [23:30] Priya: last note — if you share a sample failing trace we'll prioritize an SE deep-dive and a reproduction run.
[23:40] Maya: will do. We'll anonymize PII per your export guide.
[23:45] [24:00] Daniel: thanks everyone — this was helpful.
[24:05] Alex: thanks all, we'll send the materials.
[24:10] [end of recorded meeting]
